# Clarification register

One row per question. Questions are short, numbered and come with a proposed
default. An answer is never removed; a changed answer gets a new row that
supersedes the old one.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `open` | Asked, not answered |
| `answered` | Answered by the user; the answer is used |
| `default` | The user accepted the proposed default |
| `superseded` | Replaced by a later question (named in Answer) |
| `withdrawn` | No longer needed (reason in Answer) |

| ID | Date | Source | Question | Proposed default | Status | Answer | Used in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q-1 | | | | | open | | |

**Source** names where the question comes from: an input file and section,
an RTL file and line, or a review finding.
**Used in** names the sections, tables and figures that depend on the
answer, so that a later change can be traced.

# Checklist: intake (workflow steps 1 to 3)

## Configuration

- [ ] `project.md` exists and its `yaml` block reads without errors.
- [ ] `document_type` and `approach` have supported values.
- [ ] `document.title`, `document.short_name` and `document.author` are set.
- [ ] For `rtl`: `inputs.rtl_top` is set and the module exists in the RTL.
- [ ] The input folders exist and contain the expected files.
- [ ] `style.md` has no unknown keys and passes the contrast check (or is
      empty).
- [ ] `specforge_version` matches the framework, or the differences were
      reviewed with the user.
- [ ] `clarifications.md`, `revision-history.md` and `status.md` exist.

## Analysis

- [ ] Every input file is listed in `analysis.md` with a summary.
- [ ] For `rtl`: the RTL version (commit, tag or date) is recorded and the
      inventory was run.
- [ ] Every extracted fact has a source and a state (confirmed or derived).
- [ ] Every item of `shared/information-checklist.md` is marked given,
      partly given or missing.
- [ ] Contradictions, ambiguities and naming problems are listed as
      findings.
- [ ] The understanding is summarized for the user to confirm.

## Clarification

- [ ] Every finding that changes the document has a question.
- [ ] Every question is in `clarifications.md` with source and proposed
      default.
- [ ] Questions are short, numbered, grouped, most blocking first.
- [ ] Nothing that blocks the outline is still open.

# Checklist: before presenting a build (workflow steps 6 and 7)

## Sources

- [ ] Chapter files are named `NN_name.md`, one chapter each, in order.
- [ ] Every figure in the chapters has its source in `figures/` and an
      up-to-date SVG preview (built with `--figures`).
- [ ] No colour, font or size is set in a chapter or figure.
- [ ] Every open point in the text is listed in the constraints chapter.

## Build

- [ ] The build finishes without errors.
- [ ] No overfull boxes, undefined references or missing characters, or
      each remaining warning is explained.
- [ ] No warnings about references to items that do not exist.
- [ ] The page count is at most the maximum, or the user approved the
      exception.

## Visual check (rendered pages)

- [ ] Title page and front matter are complete and correct.
- [ ] Every page with a table or figure: nothing past the margins; labels
      readable and not overlapping.
- [ ] No heading alone at the foot of a page; figures near their first
      reference; no large empty areas.
- [ ] Header, footer and page numbers are correct.

## Content

- [ ] The acceptance criteria of the document type are met
      (`guides/design-spec/rules/04-acceptance.md`).
- [ ] `outline.md` matches the document.
===== END FILE =====

# Checklist: release (workflow step 8)

- [ ] `checklists/pre-build.md` is complete for the final build.
- [ ] All review findings are resolved or rejected with a reason in the
      review record.
- [ ] No open question in `clarifications.md` affects released content
      without being shown as an open point.
- [ ] `revision-history.md` has a row for this revision describing every
      change set since the last release.
- [ ] `project.md` has the revision, status and date of the release (or the
      date is left to the build date on purpose).
- [ ] `colour-record.md` is current for the final style.
- [ ] For `rtl`: the references name the RTL version the document describes.
- [ ] The PDF and the combined Markdown in the output folder are from the
      final build.
- [ ] The user approved the release; `status.md` records it.
- [ ] The release is committed (if the project is under Git).

===== BEGIN FILE: <specforge>/styles/style-defaults.md =====
# Style defaults

The default value of every styled element of a specforge document. The
values reproduce the reference specification that specforge was
derived from, and they follow the rules of `colour-guide.md`.

A project changes any value by naming its key, with the same nesting, in the
`overrides` block of its `style.md`. Keys that are not overridden keep the
values below. The build turns the merged values into the
LaTeX style files, so these keys are the only place where a style value is
defined.

Units are part of the key name (`_pt`, `_mm`). The tokens of the `colour`
group are `#RRGGBB`. Every other colour refers to a token by name (for
example `text_primary`), so that changing a token changes every element
that uses it; a project may instead give one element its own `#RRGGBB`.
Plain colour names for the common elements are listed in
`config-templates/style.md`. Every foreground and background pair is
contrast-checked on each build.

```yaml
page:
  paper: a4                        # a4 | letter
  class_font_size_pt: 11           # base size of the document class
  margin_mm: 22                    # all four sides
  head_height_pt: 14
  head_sep_mm: 8
  foot_skip_mm: 11
  chapter_starts_new_page: false   # chapters run on, to fit the page budget
  front_matter_numbering: roman    # title page, document information, contents
  body_numbering: arabic

colour:                            # colour-guide.md Sections 4.1, 4.3 (light theme)
  text_primary: "#202729"          # body text, headings, table text, labels
  text_secondary: "#555F5B"        # captions, header, footer, wires, sub-labels
  bg_page: "#FFFFFF"               # page background
  bg_subtle: "#F5F7F6"             # table header row, top-level boundary fill
  border_subtle: "#D6DEDA"         # decorative rules only (table rows, grids)
  border_strong: "#76817C"         # meaningful boundaries (block outlines, header rule)
  accent_primary: "#3A8760"        # graphics only: chapter rule, highlighted path
  accent_strong: "#1E4D35"         # graphics and fills
  accent_subtle: "#EAF5EE"         # background behind text (highlighted entry)
  accent_secondary: "#A9D5BD"      # decorative fills
  info_fg: "#245A8D"               # semantic colours: always with a text label
  info_bg: "#EDF4FA"
  warn_fg: "#855000"
  warn_bg: "#FFF5DF"
  error_fg: "#A52626"
  error_bg: "#FBECEC"

fonts:                             # OpenType families (colour-guide.md Section 8.1)
  main: SourceSans3                # body text
  main_upright: "*-Regular"
  main_italic: "*-RegularIt"
  main_bold: "*-Semibold"
  main_bold_italic: "*-SemiboldIt"
  heading: SourceSans3             # headings, title, block names
  heading_upright: "*-Bold"
  heading_italic: "*-BoldIt"
  mono: SourceCodePro              # signals, parameters, modules, code
  mono_upright: "*-Regular"
  mono_bold: "*-Semibold"
  mono_scale: 0.88

body:
  line_spread: 1.12
  paragraph_skip_pt: 6
  ragged_right: true               # no justified text
  hyphenation: false
  list_item_sep_pt: 2
  list_top_sep_pt: 4
  identifiers_monospace: true      # signal, parameter and module names

headings:                          # all headings in heading font, text_primary
  colour: text_primary
  chapter:
    size_pt: 19
    leading_pt: 23
    space_before_pt: 22
    space_after_pt: 10
    rule_colour: accent_primary    # short rule under the chapter title
    rule_width_mm: 20
    rule_thickness_pt: 2
  section:
    size_pt: 17
    leading_pt: 21
    space_before_pt: 20
    space_after_pt: 6
  subsection:
    size_pt: 14
    leading_pt: 17
    space_before_pt: 16
    space_after_pt: 4
  subsubsection:
    size_pt: 12
    leading_pt: 15
    space_before_pt: 12
    space_after_pt: 3
  numbering_depth: 3               # 1.2.3.4 is the deepest numbered level
  toc_depth: 0                     # contents list chapters only (page budget)

title_page:
  top_space_mm: 48
  rule_colour: accent_primary      # the only graphical marker on the page
  rule_width_mm: 24
  rule_thickness_pt: 3
  title_size_pt: 34
  title_leading_pt: 40
  title_colour: text_primary
  subtitle_size_pt: 18
  subtitle_leading_pt: 22
  subtitle_colour: text_secondary
  fields: [Author, Revision, Date, Status]   # shown at the foot of the page
  field_label_colour: text_secondary

front_matter:
  document_information: true       # table: type, design, revision, date, author, status
  revision_history: true
  contents: true
  list_of_figures: false           # omitted to fit the page budget
  list_of_tables: false
  share_one_page: true             # information, history and contents on one page if they fit

header_footer:
  font_size: small
  colour: text_secondary
  header_left: title               # title | short_name | chapter | none
  header_right: chapter
  footer_left: "Revision {revision} • {status}"
  footer_right: page
  header_rule_pt: 0.5
  header_rule_colour: border_subtle
  footer_rule_pt: 0

captions:
  font_size: small
  colour: text_secondary
  label_bold: true
  label_colour: text_primary
  label_separator: period
  skip_pt: 8
  table_caption_position: above
  figure_caption_position: below

tables:                            # colour-guide.md Sections 5.2, 11
  font_size_pt: 10
  leading_pt: 12.5
  row_stretch: 1.35
  column_sep_pt: 6
  header_fill: bg_subtle
  header_bold: true
  outer_rule_colour: border_strong # top, below header, bottom
  outer_rule_pt: 0.8
  row_rule_colour: border_subtle
  row_rule_pt: 0.5
  vertical_rules: false
  breakable: false                 # short tables, kept on one page

callouts:                          # colour-guide.md Sections 5.3, 16
  open_point:
    label: OPEN POINT
    fill: warn_bg
    bar_colour: warn_fg
    bar_width_pt: 2.4
    label_colour: warn_fg
  pending:
    label: PENDING                 # marks information not yet confirmed
    colour: warn_fg
  note:
    fill: bg_subtle                # highlighted statement (e.g. a key rule)
    width_fraction: 0.92

figures:
  max_height_fraction: 0.44        # of the text height (page budget)
  max_height_fraction_timing: 0.62 # timing diagrams need more room
  top_fraction: 0.95               # float placement: let figures share pages
  text_fraction: 0.05
  float_page_fraction: 0.8
  max_floats_per_page: 2
  floats_stay_in_chapter: true

diagrams:                          # colour-guide.md Sections 5.4, 12
  boundary:                        # top-level module boundary
    draw: border_strong
    fill: bg_subtle
    line_pt: 1.1
  block:                           # functional block
    draw: border_strong
    fill: bg_page
    line_pt: 0.9
  group:                           # interface group box
    draw: border_strong
    fill: bg_page
    line_pt: 0.8
    corner_radius_pt: 2
  wire:
    colour: text_secondary
    line_pt: 0.8
  control_wire_pt: 0.7             # control signals thin
  data_wire_pt: 1.7                # data and state signals thick
  bundle_pt: 1.3
  packet_line_pt: 0.6              # each of the two lines of a packet arrow
  packet_gap_pt: 1.6               # space between them
  highlight:                       # highlighted path, always labelled
    colour: accent_primary
    line_pt: 1.1
  port_size_mm: 2
  junction_size_mm: 1.6
  signal_label_size_pt: 8          # monospace, text_primary
  block_name_size_pt: 12           # heading font, text_primary
  block_sub_size_pt: 8.5           # text_secondary
  group_title_size_pt: 8.5
  width_label_size_pt: 8

state_machines:                    # state diagrams: circles and arrows
  state:
    draw: border_strong
    fill: accent_subtle            # text_primary on it is contrast-checked
    line_pt: 0.9
    size_mm: 13                    # smallest circle; all states the same size
  name_size_pt: 8.5                # state name, monospace
  label_size_pt: 8                 # conditions, outputs, legend
  transition:
    colour: text_secondary
    line_pt: 0.8
  reset:
    colour: text_primary           # reset entry: filled dot, thicker line
    line_pt: 1.4

timing:                            # colour-guide.md Sections 5.7, 13
  signal_colour: text_primary
  clock_colour: text_secondary
  line_pt: 0.8
  grid_colour: border_subtle
  grid_line_pt: 0.4
  undefined_pattern: hatch         # value not specified
  undefined_pattern_colour: border_strong
  label_size_pt: 8                 # monospace
  x_scale: 2.7                     # one clock cycle = two timing units
  y_scale: 1.5
  slope: 0.12

pdf:
  bookmarks_numbered: true
  display_title: true
  hide_links: true                 # links are not boxed or coloured
```

## Elements and their sources

| Group | Applies to | Base rules in `colour-guide.md` |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | Paper, margins, header and footer spacing, numbering | Sections 9, 19.3 |
| `colour` | Every colour in the document | Part II (Sections 3 to 7) |
| `fonts`, `body` | Text, identifiers | Sections 8.1 to 8.6 |
| `headings` | Chapter to subsubsection headings | Sections 5.1, 8.4 |
| `title_page`, `front_matter` | Title page, document information, revision history, contents | Sections 5.8, 10 |
| `header_footer` | Running header and footer | Section 19 |
| `captions` | Figure and table captions | Sections 12.6, 17.4 |
| `tables` | All tables | Sections 5.2, 11 |
| `state_machines` | State diagrams | Sections 5.4, 12 |
| `callouts` | Open points, pending markers, highlighted notes | Sections 5.3, 16 |
| `figures` | Figure size and placement | Section 17 |
| `diagrams` | Block and architecture diagrams | Sections 5.4, 12 |
| `timing` | Timing diagrams and waveforms | Sections 5.7, 13 |
| `pdf` | PDF properties | Section 1 (accessibility and portability) |

## Rules that are not values

These rules hold for every document, whatever the overrides:

- Colour never carries meaning alone: a highlighted path, a callout or a
  marked entry always has a text label (`colour-guide.md` Section 4.5).
- Headings and body text use only `text_primary`; the accent is used for
  graphics, never for text.
- Every foreground/background pair meets the contrast requirement of
  `colour-guide.md` Section 3.2; changed colours are checked before a build.
- Each document gets a colour specification record
  (`colour-guide.md` Section 7.4).

===== BEGIN FILE: <specforge>/latex/README.md =====
# specforge LaTeX build

Turns a project's Markdown chapters and TikZ figures into the PDF, using the
merged style (defaults plus the project's `style.md`).

## Build

```
specforge build <project> [--figures]
specforge check <project>
```

- `--figures` also exports every `figures/*.tex` to `figures/*.svg`, so that
  the Markdown chapters show the figures. Run it whenever a figure changes.
- `check` writes only the combined Markdown and runs no LaTeX.

Requirements: LuaLaTeX, which includes `texlua`; `pdftocairo` for the
previews; the fonts named in the style. See `USER-GUIDE.md`.

## What the build does

| Step | Output |
|---|---|
| Check `project.md` and `style.md`, derive accent tokens, check contrast | `build/style-report.md` |
| Chapters and front matter to LaTeX, as data only | `build/sf-*.tex` |
| Combined Markdown | `<output.dir>/<file_name>.md` |
| Check figure sources against the allowed commands | errors with file and line |
| Figure previews (`--figures`) | `figures/*.svg` |
| Compile three times in a temporary folder, check log and page count | `build/main.log`, `<output.dir>/<file_name>.pdf` |

The build stops on any configuration error, unknown style key, failed
contrast pair, unsupported Markdown, or heading or caption number out of
sequence, and names the file and line. It warns about every reference in
the text ("Table 3.1", "Section 2.4", "Figure 1.2", "Chapter 5") that names
an item the document does not contain; a reference to another document is
written with that document's name first ("ABC Section 1.2") and is skipped.

## Project files the build reads

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `project.md` | Configuration (from `config-templates/`) |
| `style.md` | Style overrides (from `config-templates/`) |
| `revision-history.md` | Revision table (from `templates/`) |
| `chapters/NN_name.md` | One chapter per file, `NN` = 01, 02, ... in reading order |
| `figures/NAME.tex` | One TikZ picture per file (`tikzpicture` or `tikztimingtable`) |

The front matter (document information, revision history) is generated from
`project.md` and `revision-history.md`; there is no front-matter chapter
file.

## Markdown accepted in chapter files

| Markdown | Result |
|---|---|
| `# N. Title`, `## N.M Title`, `### N.M.K Title` | Chapter, section, subsection; numbers are checked |
| Paragraphs, `-` and `1.` lists (nested by two spaces) | Text and lists |
| `**Table N.M.** caption` line, then a table | Table with its caption above |
| `![alt](../figures/NAME.svg)`, then `**Figure N.M.** caption` | Figure from `figures/NAME.tex`, caption below |
| `> **Open point ID.** text` | OPEN POINT callout |
| `> text` | Highlighted statement |
| `` `code` ``, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `[text](url)` | Inline formatting; code is set in the monospace font |

A `|` inside a table cell is written in backticks or as `\|`. LaTeX in
chapter text is printed as text, never executed.

Code blocks and level-4 headings are rejected. Figures named `fig-wave-*`
or `fig-timing-*` are treated as timing diagrams (larger height limit).

## Template and styles

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `template/main.tex` | Document skeleton |
| `template/preamble/` | Packages, typography, tables, macros, title page, front matter. Every value comes from a `\sf...` macro generated from the style keys |
| `tikz/sf-tikz.tex` | Diagram styles (`boundary`, `block`, `wire`, `ctrlarrow`, `dataarrow`, `hlarrow`, `port`, ...) and the timing style `sfwave` with `\wavecycles` and `\wavenote` |

Macro names follow the style keys: `headings.chapter.size_pt` becomes
`\sfHeadingsChapterSizePt`, and a true/false key such as
`body.ragged_right` becomes the conditional `\ifsfBodyRaggedRight`.

The tool is in `tools/` at the top of the specforge folder; it runs on
texlua and needs nothing else.
===== END FILE =====

===== BEGIN FILE: <specforge>/latex/tikz/sf-tikz.tex =====
% =============================================================================
% specforge -- TikZ style library for block diagrams and timing diagrams.
% colour-guide.md Sections 5.4, 5.7, 12 and 13. Colours and line widths come
% from build/sf-config.tex (styles/style-defaults.md, groups diagrams and
% timing); shapes and arrow tips are fixed here.
%
% Block diagrams
%   boundary      top-level module boundary            block     functional block
%   ifgroup       interface-group box                  port      port square on a boundary
%   wire          plain connection                     sigarrow  connection with arrow
%   ctrl/ctrlarrow  control signal (thin)              data/dataarrow  data or state (thick)
%   bundle/bundlearrow  signal bundle or information flow  hlarrow  highlighted path (label it!)
%   packet/packetarrow  one packet (struct, interface): one arrow, no fields
%   junction, djunction  wire junctions (thin, thick)  zoomline  zoom guide (dashed)
%   siglabel  signal name     flowlabel  information in words
%   blockname / modname  block / module name
%   blocksub  block sub-label grouptitle           group title     widthlabel  bus width
% State machines (see latex-document rule 04)
%   fsmstate   state: a circle, never a box       fsmresetdot, fsmreset  reset entry
%   fsmtrans   state transition (straight, bend left/right, loop above/...)
%   fsmcond    transition label: condition / outputs
%   fsminput, fsmoutput  signals entering or leaving the machine (dashed)
%   \fsmout{text}  outputs inside a state circle (below the name)
%   \fsmlegend{(x,y)}, \fsmlegendio{(x,y)}  legend of the arrow kinds
% Buffer and pointer illustrations
%   entry, entryhl (highlighted), entrydim (invalid), entrywarn (warning; label it)
%   ptrarrow  pointer arrow   rangebrace  brace under a range of entries
% Timing diagrams (tikz-timing)
%   style sfwave on the tikztimingtable; \wavecycles{n} draws the cycle grid
%   and numbers, \wavenote{first}{last}{text} adds a note under cycles.
%   One clock cycle is two timing units wide; the clock row is [sfclock]4{HL}.
%   Ragged-right text distorts tikz-timing tables: the build wraps every
%   figure named fig-wave-* or fig-timing-* in justified text.
% =============================================================================
\usetikzlibrary{arrows.meta,calc,positioning,patterns,backgrounds,
                decorations.pathreplacing}

% ---- Timing diagrams ----------------------------------------------------------
% Font of size #1 pt with 1.2 x leading.
\newcommand{\sfsize}[1]{\fontsize{#1}{\fpeval{1.2*(#1)}}\selectfont}
\newcommand{\wavefont}{\ttfamily\sfsize{\sfTimingLabelSizePt}}
\tikzset{
  sfwave/.style={
    xscale=\sfTimingXScale, yscale=\sfTimingYScale,
    line width=\sfTimingLinePt pt, color=\sfTimingSignalColour,
    timing/slope=\sfTimingSlope,
    timing/rowdist=2,
    timing/name/.style={font=\wavefont, text=\sfTimingSignalColour},
    timing/d/text/.style={font=\wavefont, text=\sfTimingSignalColour},
    timing/d/background/.style={fill=bgpage},
    timing/u/.style={draw=\sfTimingClockColour},
    timing/u/background/.style={pattern=north east lines,
                                pattern color=\sfTimingUndefinedPatternColour},
  },
  % Row option for the clock: [sfclock]4{HL}
  sfclock/.style={color=\sfTimingClockColour},
  wavecycle/.style={font=\sfsize{\sfTimingLabelSizePt},
                    text=textsecondary, inner sep=1pt},
  wavenote/.style={font=\sfsize{\sfTimingLabelSizePt},
                   text=textprimary, inner sep=1pt, align=center},
}

% Cycle grid and cycle numbers. #1 = number of cycles shown.
\newcommand{\wavecycles}[1]{%
  \begin{scope}[on background layer]
    \foreach \c in {0,...,#1} {
      \draw[\sfTimingGridColour, line width=\sfTimingGridLinePt pt]
        (2*\c,1.45) -- (2*\c,-2*\nrows+1.75);
    }
  \end{scope}
  \foreach \c in {1,...,#1} {
    \node[wavecycle] at (2*\c-1,1.85) {\the\numexpr\c-1\relax};
  }
  \node[wavecycle, anchor=east] at (-0.35,1.85) {cycle};
}

% Text note under the waveform. #1 = first cycle, #2 = last cycle, #3 = text.
\newcommand{\wavenote}[3]{%
  \node[wavenote, anchor=north] at (#1+#2+1,-2*\nrows+1.6) {#3};
}

% ---- Block diagrams -----------------------------------------------------------
\tikzset{
  boundary/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsBoundaryDraw, fill=\sfDiagramsBoundaryFill,
                   line width=\sfDiagramsBoundaryLinePt pt},
  block/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsBlockDraw, fill=\sfDiagramsBlockFill,
                line width=\sfDiagramsBlockLinePt pt, rectangle},
  ifgroup/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsGroupDraw, fill=\sfDiagramsGroupFill,
                  line width=\sfDiagramsGroupLinePt pt,
                  rounded corners=\sfDiagramsGroupCornerRadiusPt pt},
  wire/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsWireColour, line width=\sfDiagramsWireLinePt pt,
               line cap=round, line join=round},
  sigarrow/.style={wire, -{Stealth[length=2.3mm,width=1.7mm]}},
  ctrl/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsWireColour, line width=\sfDiagramsControlWirePt pt,
               line cap=round, line join=round},
  ctrlarrow/.style={ctrl, -{Stealth[length=2.2mm,width=1.6mm]}},
  data/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsWireColour, line width=\sfDiagramsDataWirePt pt,
               line join=round},
  dataarrow/.style={data, -{Stealth[length=3.2mm,width=2.6mm]}},
  bundle/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsWireColour, line width=\sfDiagramsBundlePt pt,
                 line cap=butt},
  bundlearrow/.style={bundle, -{Stealth[length=2.8mm,width=2.2mm]}},
  % one packet (struct, interface, field group) as a whole: double line,
  % open head; its fields are never drawn
  packet/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsWireColour, line width=\sfDiagramsPacketLinePt pt,
                 double=bgpage, double distance=\sfDiagramsPacketGapPt pt, line cap=butt},
  packetarrow/.style={packet, -{Latex[open, length=3.4mm, width=3.2mm, line width=\sfDiagramsPacketLinePt pt]}},
  hlarrow/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsHighlightColour,
                  line width=\sfDiagramsHighlightLinePt pt, line join=round,
                  -{Stealth[length=2.5mm,width=1.9mm]}},
  port/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsBoundaryDraw, fill=bgpage,
               line width=\sfDiagramsWireLinePt pt, rectangle,
               minimum size=\sfDiagramsPortSizeMm mm, inner sep=0pt},
  junction/.style={circle, fill=\sfDiagramsWireColour, draw=none,
                   minimum size=\sfDiagramsJunctionSizeMm mm, inner sep=0pt},
  djunction/.style={junction, minimum size=1.5*\sfDiagramsJunctionSizeMm mm},
  zoomline/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsBoundaryDraw, line width=0.7pt,
                   dash pattern=on 3pt off 2pt},
  siglabel/.style={font=\ttfamily\sfsize{\sfDiagramsSignalLabelSizePt},
                   text=textprimary, inner sep=1.6pt},
  blockname/.style={font=\headingfont\sfsize{\sfDiagramsBlockNameSizePt},
                    text=textprimary, align=center},
  modname/.style={font=\headingfont\sfsize{\fpeval{\sfDiagramsBlockNameSizePt-1}},
                  text=textprimary, align=center},
  blocksub/.style={font=\sfsize{\sfDiagramsBlockSubSizePt},
                   text=textsecondary, align=center},
  grouptitle/.style={font=\bfseries\sfsize{\sfDiagramsGroupTitleSizePt},
                     text=textprimary, inner sep=1.6pt},
  % what an information flow carries, in words (not a signal name)
  flowlabel/.style={font=\sfsize{\sfDiagramsSignalLabelSizePt},
                    text=textprimary, inner sep=1.6pt},
  widthlabel/.style={font=\sfsize{\sfDiagramsWidthLabelSizePt},
                     text=textsecondary, inner sep=1.6pt},
}

% ---- Buffer and pointer illustrations ----------------------------------------
\tikzset{
  entry/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsBlockDraw, fill=bgpage,
                line width=\sfDiagramsWireLinePt pt, rectangle,
                minimum width=9mm, minimum height=7mm, inner sep=0pt,
                font=\wavefont, text=textprimary},
  entryhl/.style={entry, draw=\sfDiagramsHighlightColour, fill=accentsubtle,
                  line width=1.2pt},
  entrydim/.style={entry, fill=bgsubtle, draw=bordersubtle, text=textsecondary},
  entrywarn/.style={entry, draw=warnfg, fill=warnbg, line width=1.2pt},
  ptrarrow/.style={wire, -{Stealth[length=2.3mm,width=1.7mm]}},
  rangebrace/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsWireColour, line width=\sfDiagramsWireLinePt pt,
                     decorate, decoration={brace, amplitude=5pt, mirror}},
}

% ---- State machines -------------------------------------------------------------
% States are circles. Transitions are filled-head arrows, straight or bent;
% the reset entry starts at a filled dot; signals into or out of the
% machine are dashed. Colours and sizes come from the state_machines keys.
\tikzset{
  fsmstate/.style={circle, draw=\sfStateMachinesStateDraw, fill=\sfStateMachinesStateFill,
                   line width=\sfStateMachinesStateLinePt pt,
                   minimum size=\sfStateMachinesStateSizeMm mm, inner sep=1pt, align=center,
                   font=\ttfamily\sfsize{\sfStateMachinesNameSizePt}, text=textprimary},
  fsmtrans/.style={draw=\sfStateMachinesTransitionColour,
                   line width=\sfStateMachinesTransitionLinePt pt,
                   -{Stealth[length=2.4mm,width=1.8mm]}, shorten >=0.4pt,
                   every loop/.style={looseness=6, min distance=8mm}},
  fsmresetdot/.style={circle, fill=\sfStateMachinesResetColour, draw=none,
                      minimum size=2.2mm, inner sep=0pt},
  fsmreset/.style={draw=\sfStateMachinesResetColour, line width=\sfStateMachinesResetLinePt pt,
                   -{Stealth[length=2.8mm,width=2.2mm]}, shorten >=0.4pt},
  fsmcond/.style={font=\ttfamily\sfsize{\sfStateMachinesLabelSizePt}, text=textprimary,
                  fill=bgpage, inner sep=1pt, align=center},
  fsminput/.style={draw=\sfDiagramsWireColour, line width=\sfDiagramsWireLinePt pt,
                   dash pattern=on 3pt off 2pt, -{Stealth[length=2.2mm,width=1.6mm]}},
  fsmoutput/.style={fsminput},
}
% Outputs inside a state circle, below the name (Moore outputs).
\newcommand{\fsmout}[1]{\\{\color{textsecondary}\sfsize{\sfStateMachinesLabelSizePt}#1}}
% Legend: reset entry and transition; #1 = top left corner, e.g. (0,-3).
\newcommand{\fsmlegend}[1]{%
  \begin{scope}[shift={#1}]
    \node[fsmresetdot] (fsmlgdot) at (0,0) {};
    \draw[fsmreset] (fsmlgdot) -- (0.9,0);
    \node[flowlabel, anchor=west] at (1.0,0) {reset};
    \draw[fsmtrans] (0,-0.55) -- (0.9,-0.55);
    \node[flowlabel, anchor=west] at (1.0,-0.55) {transition: condition / outputs};
  \end{scope}}
% Legend with the dashed inputs and outputs of the machine as well.
\newcommand{\fsmlegendio}[1]{%
  \fsmlegend{#1}%
  \begin{scope}[shift={#1}]
    \draw[fsminput] (0,-1.1) -- (0.9,-1.1);
    \node[flowlabel, anchor=west] at (1.0,-1.1) {input or output signal};
  \end{scope}}
